Representative character-chat detail and primary conversation journey.
Image-generation tool archetype and mobile interactive flow.

findings.summary: The site hard-codes a dark presentation instead of adapting to the user’s colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The normal desktop capture is dark, while raw server HTML contains no prefers-color-scheme or color-scheme handling.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light and dark tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Reduced-motion preferences are not implemented.
findings.evidence: Raw server HTML and inline styles contain no prefers-reduced-motion rule; the reduced-motion capture was additionally blocked by the edge WAF, so static authored output is the direct signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap non-essential transitions and animation in no-preference queries and remove or shorten them under reduce.

findings.summary: Some text fails minimum contrast and there is no high-contrast adaptation.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a failing colour-contrast node (.fc-faq-label), and raw output contains no prefers-contrast or forced-colors handling.
findings.suggestedFix: Raise text contrast and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations without suppressing system colours.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: Raw rendered HTML contains no view-transition declarations, while this SPA exposes route changes between discovery, generator, chat and membership surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for SPA route/state changes, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: A consent wall obscures the entire experience on every tested path.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a full-screen dimmer and consent modal before any interaction; on mobile it occupies almost the full viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the full takeover with a compact, accessible consent surface that leaves essential content available and includes equally prominent choices.

findings.summary: Overlays are implemented as custom/non-semantic surfaces and can render blank.
findings.evidence: Raw output contains no dialog or popover primitive; the chat screenshot shows a blank white modal panel over the conversation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog/popover semantics with labelled content, focus management, Escape/light-dismiss where appropriate, and a robust loading/error state.

findings.summary: Reusable cards and navigation rely on viewport styling rather than container responsiveness.
findings.evidence: The SSR output contains no @container or container-type despite card components being reused in desktop grids and mobile feeds.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable card/navigation wrappers containment and adapt internals with size container queries.

findings.summary: Mobile icon navigation has unnamed interactive targets.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found four links without discernible names in the mobile footer navigation, preventing reliable keyboard and assistive interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Add visible or aria-label names, preserve visible focus, and keep touch targets at least 44 CSS pixels.

findings.summary: The consent wall prevents the primary chat, image-generation and membership journeys from starting.
findings.evidence: All four representative path screenshots are covered by the consent surface; the chat path additionally shows a blank modal.
findings.suggestedFix: Let users reject or configure non-essential processing without blocking core use, then test chat and generation end to end.

findings.summary: Blocked and failed states do not provide useful recovery.
findings.evidence: The discoverability browser capture intermittently receives EdgeOne “Restricted Access 567” with only an owner-oriented instruction, and the chat overlay is blank.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a user-facing retry/back route and support reference for WAF blocks, plus explicit loading and error content in overlays.

findings.summary: Mobile loading performance is poor.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 20.8 s, FCP 3.9 s, TBT 700 ms and a performance score of 0.40; a separate trace measured LCP 2.25 s, showing high run-to-run variability.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, delay non-essential third parties, and reduce initial JavaScript execution.

findings.summary: Initial JavaScript work blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 700 ms TBT; 71 scripts were transferred in the HAR.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or defer non-critical scripts, split long tasks, and schedule background work at lower priority.

findings.summary: The critical network path is long and cache/render delivery is inefficient.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 173 requests and 2.23 MB, including ten parser-inserted high-priority stylesheets; Lighthouse reports a 6.1 s dependency chain and about 500 ms render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, consolidate/defer the rest, apply durable caching to hashed assets, and prioritise only true critical resources.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused JavaScript and CSS ship on first load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 572 KiB unused JavaScript and 42 KiB unused CSS, including advertising, tag-manager and app bundles.
findings.suggestedFix: Use route-level code splitting and conditionally load advertising/analytics after consent and when needed.

findings.summary: Several interactive links lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility reports four unnamed mobile footer links; the images primitive also reports eight images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Name every icon link and supply meaningful alt text, or empty alt for decorative images.

findings.summary: Consent/help text has insufficient colour contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identifies .fc-faq-label as failing the colour-contrast audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG AA in every consent and helper-text state.

findings.summary: The viewport explicitly prevents user zoom.
findings.evidence: The page ships maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=no; Lighthouse fails the meta-viewport accessibility audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and user-scalable restrictions and verify reflow at 200–400% zoom.

findings.summary: The page is not eligible for back/forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports one BFCache restoration failure even though deprecation and inspector audits pass.
findings.suggestedFix: Inspect the BFCache not-restored reason and remove unload handlers or other blockers.

findings.summary: One account-management action is not a crawlable link and the viewport is not zoom-friendly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports an anchor.delete-account without href and fails the restrictive viewport audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href destinations for navigation and an unrestricted responsive viewport.

findings.summary: The advertised sitemap endpoint serves a soft 404 document.
findings.evidence: GET /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 200 but HTML whose title/canonical/hreflang all describe /404 rather than XML.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid XML sitemap with an XML content type and a truthful non-200 status for missing resources.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no CSP or X-Content-Type-Options; all 12 observed cookies lack Secure and most use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash CSP, nosniff, and Secure/SameSite-appropriate cookie attributes; keep HSTS and SAMEORIGIN.

findings.summary: Tracking executes before an informed consent choice.
findings.evidence: HAR records 170/173 requests and 2.19 MB as non-main-origin, including Google Ads/Analytics and Facebook; trackers evidence finds four known trackers while the consent wall is still on screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Block advertising and analytics tags until an explicit opt-in, minimise vendors, shorten retention, and batch essential telemetry.

findings.summary: No phishing-resistant authentication capability is exposed.
findings.evidence: The public SSR output has a Log In route but no WebAuthn, PublicKeyCredential or navigator.credentials integration; no permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and sign-in alongside recovery, and continue requesting permissions only from user gestures.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are missing.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no CSP, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or X-Content-Type-Options; HSTS and X-Frame-Options are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP frame-ancestors/Trusted Types where feasible, strict referrer and permissions policies, and nosniff.

findings.summary: The chat route can leave an empty modal covering the application.
findings.evidence: The chat screenshot shows a large blank white overlay with no label, loading status, close affordance or recovery copy.
findings.suggestedFix: Make overlay state explicit and atomic: render labelled loading, success and error states, always with a working close/back action.

findings.summary: The app advertises a manifest but has no observable offline worker/fallback.
findings.evidence: HAR loads /manifest.webmanifest, while SSR output contains no service-worker registration and WAF/network failures replace the app with a dead-end page.
findings.suggestedFix: Register a service worker for a small offline shell and recovery page, and verify manifest installability.

findings.summary: Network/security failures produce a dead end rather than a recoverable app state.
findings.evidence: The rendered discoverability capture shows Restricted Access 567 and tells the user only to contact the owner; no retry, home or support action is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide retry, return-home and support actions while preserving context; return truthful HTTP statuses.

findings.summary: Consent is not a balanced, informed choice and trackers run before it.
findings.evidence: The first layer offers Consent and Manage options but no equally prominent Reject all; HAR simultaneously records Google/Facebook advertising and analytics requests before choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Present Accept and Reject all with equal prominence, default non-essential purposes off, and do not fire vendors before opt-in.

findings.summary: The blank chat modal gives no error explanation or recovery.
findings.evidence: The chat screenshot contains an empty white panel over dimmed content with no status text or actionable control.
findings.suggestedFix: Render accessible status/error text, move focus to it, and provide retry/cancel without losing chat context.

findings.summary: Consent blocks pricing/account evaluation and the membership path renders no product context behind it.
findings.evidence: The membership screenshot is an otherwise blank black page beneath the consent wall, so pricing, commitment and cancellation information are unavailable.
findings.suggestedFix: Render essential pricing and account terms independently of marketing consent, with clear cancellation and confirmation steps.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not consistently responsive or right-sized.
findings.evidence: Images evidence finds 10 oversized images, 42 without srcset and 7 legacy-format assets; 55 images lack width/height attributes even where CSS may reserve space.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate srcset/sizes variants, keep modern formats, set intrinsic dimensions and lazy-load below-fold media.

findings.summary: The page performs substantial non-essential work before consent.
findings.evidence: HAR records 71 scripts and 170 non-main-origin requests; Lighthouse estimates 572 KiB unused JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate analytics/ads, conditionally import features, and defer low-value fetches until idle or user intent.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates the page budget.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 2.19 MB of 2.23 MB transferred to non-main origins, with GTM, Facebook and AdSense among the largest scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove redundant vendors and load retained integrations only after consent and interaction.

findings.summary: The AI service exposes no structured browser-agent capability.
findings.evidence: SSR output contains no WebMCP or agentic form/tool declarations despite chat and image generation being suitable structured tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Pilot narrowly scoped WebMCP tools for character search and draft generation with confirmation before side effects.

findings.summary: No on-device inference path is offered for lightweight AI tasks.
findings.evidence: SSR output contains no built-in LanguageModel or Summarizer integration; all product intelligence is server-oriented.
findings.suggestedFix: Consider optional on-device summarisation or drafting where capability detection and privacy benefits justify it.
